answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable bond that is slashed when peers prove misbehavior. Like basalt foundations under a terrace, the bond makes every new identity expensive to create and cheap to lose: an attacker must fund thousands of bonds, while honest agents keep one. A shared reef of attestations then tracks behavior over time, so a fresh identity cannot buy instant trust; it must earn standing through verified work, and losing it forfeits the bond.
